statement: The GP referral presented one integrated problem beginning with painful abnormal feet and gait and escalating into pathological neurological signs, rather than two already-separated pathways.
challenges: The evidence does not establish one exclusive mechanism for every structural foot lesion.

statement: The surviving admission record shows asymmetric clinical weighting: the findings pointing toward severe very-young-onset Parkinsonism/PRKN were investigated and elaborated far more completely than the painful abnormal feet and gait problem through which the referral began.
challenges: This does not prove that the neurologist failed to read the referral or acted unreasonably in initially prioritising the striking neurological syndrome.

statement: Before closure the patient directly said, in substance, that the feet had not been properly dealt with and the neurological work could not therefore be complete; the Protest restored the underweighted first paragraph of the GP referral rather than introducing a new problem or contesting a separation the patient already understood.

The neurologist answered Podiatry; the record identifies no neurological reopening and no defined neurological handover carrying the restored feet–neurology question into Podiatry. Initial narrowing may have been understandable; after the Protest the originating problem was expressly back in view before closure.
challenges: Podiatry could appropriately treat structural manifestations; the issue is what Neurology did once the originating referral problem was expressly restored to view.

statement: The discharge synthesis is the founding join: it contains the dystonic-looking lower-limb, structural-foot, Parkinsonism and PRKN/PARK2 material, then allocates the painful feet principally to a separate/peripheral-neuropathy/Podiatry channel ending 'Not clear' while Parkinsonism/PRKN receives much richer explanatory development.
challenges: The synthesis does not state that the feet are definitively non-neurological; the issue is the direction and operational effect of the join it constructs.

statement: The founding synthesis strengthens patient-derived separation by recording that he had 'in his own mind - markedly divorced' leg tension from foot pain/corns/callouses, while the Protest showing that he had restored the originating foot problem as unfinished is absent from the portable account.
challenges: The underlying patient-origin phenomenological distinction and clinician-authored intensification must remain distinct.

statement: The final portable synthesis preserves the selected management architecture and compatible patient knowledge-state while omitting the event that explains why the original referral problem had to be reconsidered before closure.
challenges: No inference of private motive is required.

statement: Later treatment states and independent clinical observations repeatedly cross the boundaries of the 2017 founding join, including procyclidine withdrawal, recurrent focal foot loading, GP reintegration, OFF-related pain/shuffling and dopaminergic relief.
challenges: These observations test the adequacy and durability of the founding arrangement; they do not by themselves prove one exclusive mechanism.

statement: Podiatry acquired local mechanical information while Neurology acquired dynamic treatment-state information; the founding join already existed in the discharge synthesis, but the record identifies no later formal re-join that reconstructs that synthesis against the two streams of evidence.
challenges: This is an information-flow conclusion, not a claim that either specialty alone could establish the full mechanism.

statement: The record identifies repeated local updates but no identified global reconstruction that resets the 2017 directional join against accumulating later evidence.
challenges: The audit remains open to any candidate reconstructive document produced later.

statement: In 2025 historical letters and claimed longstanding shared understanding were invoked to answer a challenge to the historical pathway itself.
challenges: Later letters may accurately prove later events; continuity alone is not independent proof that the founding representation was complete or appropriately reconstructed.

statement: By the time of the Protest, substantial diagnostic, hierarchical and therapeutic commitment had accumulated around the young-onset Parkinsonism/PRKN formulation, creating an objective professional-coherence or commitment-pressure context when the patient restored the underweighted part of the referral.
challenges: This is not proof of pride, embarrassment, deliberate concealment or any other private motive.
